info.title: curio
info.description: curio - the Curiosity Workspace admin sandbox (the one Sudo works in) from your terminal: sessions, the shell, the commit review loop, JSON output for scripts and coding agents, and a two-panel file manager (curio tui).

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
curio - the Curiosity Workspace admin sandbox from your terminal.

Run a command: curio run -- <command line>. Open the two-panel interface (for people, never for scripts or coding agents): curio tui.
For scripts and coding agents: pass --json and --yes, start long commands with run --detach, and wait with --timeout.

Exit codes: 0 done | 1 failed or discarded | 64 usage, or a question that needs --yes | 75 conflict | 77 not signed in | 78 not allowed | 79 commit awaiting approval | 124 timed out, still running or pending.
curio run passes the sandbox command's own exit code through.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --server
options.description: Workspace address, e.g. https://my-workspace.curiosity.ai (default: the current one, or CURIOSITY_SERVER)

options.name: --session
options.description: Session id or name (default: the last one used on this workspace, or CURIO_SESSION)

options.name: --insecure
options.description: Do not verify the workspace's TLS certificate, for HTTP and WebSocket connections alike (self-signed or internal CAs; or CURIO_INSECURE=1) [default: False]

options.name: --json
options.description: Write the answer as one line of JSON on standard output, and errors as JSON on standard error; never ask a question (see the Readme for the shapes) [default: False]

options.name: --yes
options.description: Answer yes to the confirmation of a destructive command (session rm and reset, commit approve and discard). Without a terminal, and with --json, those commands stop with exit 64 unless it is given. Accepted by every command [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Seconds before curio gives up (0 = no limit; or CURIO_TIMEOUT). Without a terminal the default is 120 (900 for run, export, upload, put, get and approving); at a terminal there is none. For run wait and commit wait it is how long to wait: exit 124 when it passes.

commands.name: login
commands.description: Sign in through the browser. Asks for the workspace address when none is given, and whether curio may approve changes.

options.name: --store
options.description: Where to keep the token: auto (keyring, else file), keyring, file or none [default: auto]

options.name: --no-browser
options.description: Print the sign-in link instead of opening a browser [default: False]

options.name: --approve
options.description: Ask for the right to approve and apply changes from curio (the sign-in page still decides) [default: False]

options.name: --no-approve
options.description: Approve changes in the browser instead; do not ask [default: False]

commands.name: logout
commands.description: Sign out of the workspace and forget the stored token

commands.name: whoami
commands.description: Show the workspace, the account and the session in use

commands.name: sessions
commands.description: List, create, pick, rename and delete sessions. Each one is a Sudo conversation with its own sandbox.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the sessions on this workspace

commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a session and make it the current one

commands.name: use
commands.description: Make a session the current one

commands.name: rename
commands.description: Rename the current session (or --session)

commands.name: rm
commands.description: Delete the current session (or --session): the conversation, and every uncommitted change in its sandbox

commands.name: reset
commands.description: Throw away every uncommitted change in the session's sandbox

commands.name: stop
commands.description: Stop whatever the session is running - a command, or Sudo's turn

commands.name: run
commands.description: Run a command (or a script) in the session's sandbox; its output and exit code are passed through. To run a sandbox command that is named status, logs, wait or list, put -- first: curio run -- status

options.name: --file
options.description: Run a script file instead ('-' reads standard input)

options.name: --detach
options.description: Start the command in the sandbox and return its run id at once, without waiting. Follow it with curio run status|wait|logs <id> [default: False]

arguments.name: COMMAND
arguments.description: The command line to run in the sandbox, e.g. curio run -- ls -la /workspace

commands.name: status
commands.description: Say whether a detached run is still going, and how it ended. Exits 0 whenever it could ask; wait is the one that passes the exit code through

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The run id curio run --detach printed

commands.name: logs
commands.description: Print what a detached run printed: standard output on standard output, standard error on standard error. The sandbox hands the output over when the command ends, so a run still going has none yet

options.name: --tail
options.description: Only the last N lines of each of standard output and standard error

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The run id curio run --detach printed

commands.name: wait
commands.description: Wait for a detached run, for --timeout seconds at most (default 120 without a terminal). When it ended: its output, and its exit code passed through. When the time ran out first: exit 124 and the run keeps going - ask again

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: The run id curio run --detach printed

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the commands this session started with --detach

commands.name: runs
commands.description: List the commands this session started with run --detach (the same as: curio run list)

commands.name: status
commands.description: List the files this session changed, and the commit waiting for approval

commands.name: diff
commands.description: Print this session's changes as unified diffs

commands.name: commit
commands.description: Review, approve or discard the commit staged in the session (stage one with: curio run -- commit -m "...")

commands.name: show
commands.description: Print the staged commit and its diff

commands.name: approve
commands.description: Apply the staged commit to the workspace. A sign-in that may not approve opens the review in the browser and waits for the answer there (for --timeout seconds; use --no-wait to return at once). Exit: 0 applied, 1 discarded or failed, 75 files changed meanwhile, 79 pending (--no-wait), 124 still waiting

options.name: --no-wait
options.description: When the approval happens in the browser: print the review link and the state, and exit 79 at once instead of waiting for the answer (then: curio commit wait --timeout N) [default: False]

options.name: --no-browser
options.description: Do not open the review in a browser; the link is printed either way [default: False]

commands.name: discard
commands.description: Throw the staged commit away; the edits stay in the sandbox

commands.name: wait
commands.description: Wait for the staged commit to be answered, for --timeout seconds at most (default 120 without a terminal), and exit with how it went: 0 applied, 1 discarded or failed, 124 still unanswered. The answer is pushed over the session's live connection; nothing polls

arguments.name: COMMIT
arguments.description: The commit id curio commit approve --no-wait printed (default: the commit waiting now)

commands.name: ls
commands.description: List a sandbox directory, marking the files this session changed

commands.name: cat
commands.description: Print a sandbox file (with --json: its text, or base64 when it is not UTF-8)

commands.name: get
commands.description: Download a sandbox file

arguments.name: LOCAL
arguments.description: Local file or folder (default: the current folder)

commands.name: put
commands.description: Write a local file into the sandbox - an uncommitted edit, like any other

options.name: --expected-hash
options.description: Refuse the write unless the sandbox file still has this hash (printed by curio get); "" = must not exist

arguments.name: REMOTE
arguments.description: Sandbox path; a directory keeps the file's name

commands.name: rm
commands.description: Delete a sandbox file - an uncommitted edit, like any other

options.name: --recursive
options.description: Delete a directory with everything in it [default: False]

commands.name: upload
commands.description: Attach local files to the session; they appear under /home/uploads

commands.name: export
commands.description: Export the workspace's definitions - endpoints, AI tools, agents, skills, schemas, indexes, tasks, NLP - the same zip as Export in Manage

options.name: --file
options.description: Save the zip here; a folder keeps the workspace's name for it (default: the current folder)

options.name: --path
options.description: Unpack the export into this folder instead, overwriting the files it carries

options.name: --prune
options.description: With --path: also delete the files under the export's folders (code/, config/, nlp/) that it no longer carries [default: False]

commands.name: skills
commands.description: The skills Sudo reads - built in and the workspace's own. They stay on the workspace: list and search them, and read one when you need it

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the skills: name, kind and what each is for

options.name: --all
options.description: Also list the skills that travel with another (the one they travel with names them) [default: False]

commands.name: search
commands.description: Search the skills without reading them all; best match first, with the passage that matched. Exit 1 when nothing matches

options.name: --limit
options.description: How many matches to show (default 10, at most 50) [default: 10]

arguments.name: QUERY
arguments.description: Words to look for in a skill's name, description and body; every word has to appear

commands.name: show
commands.description: Print one skill, as Sudo reads it

commands.name: install
commands.description: Add the curio skill to a coding agent's skills folder: how to work on this workspace through curio, the index of Sudo's skills, and how to read one. Run again to update the index.

options.name: --global
options.description: Add it to ~/.claude/skills, for every project on this machine [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite it even when it was edited since it was installed [default: False]

arguments.name: FOLDER
arguments.description: The skills folder to add curio to (default: ./.claude/skills)

commands.name: tui
commands.description: Open the two-panel interface: a full-screen terminal UI for people. Never run it from a script or a coding agent - it needs a terminal and takes it over.
